jurisdiction.name: Ukraine
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ukraine governs AI mainly through soft law. The Cabinet's 2020 Concept for the Development of AI and its action plans set the policy framework; the digital transformation ministry's 2023 bottom-up regulation roadmap and 2024 White Paper lead towards a law aligned with the EU AI Act, which is still a draft. The ministry has issued a growing set of non-binding sectoral recommendations, covering media, advertising, intellectual property, higher education, lawyers, HR, responsible AI development with human-rights impact assessment, AI agents and psychological well-being, and since 2026 the State Service of Special Communications has issued guidance on cyber protection of AI systems. A draft AI Development Strategy to 2030 went to public consultation in June 2026.
lead_institutions: State Service of Special Communications and Information Protection
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 13 October 2026 and redone in a longer review the same day, covering the digital transformation ministry's AI portal, Parliament's bills system, the Cabinet, each ministry and each sector regulator. The data protection law and the Convention 108 ratification law (Law 2438-VI of 2010, taken from Parliament's bill record) are still to be read, and a deepfake fraud bill, the energy ministry's draft AI concept, the National Bank's discussion paper and the ministry's sandbox are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: Про схвалення Концепції розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні
instruments.english_title: On approval of the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine (Cabinet of Ministers Order No. 1556-r of 2 December 2020)
instruments.current_status: In force (zakon.rada.gov.ua: 'чинний', current edition of 29.12.2021, amended by Cabinet Order No. 1787-r). Implementation is planned to 2030. The draft Cabinet order on the AI Development Strategy to 2030 put to consultation on 15 June 2026 proposes to repeal this order and its action plans; not yet adopted as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Cabinet order approving Ukraine's AI Concept, which defines artificial intelligence and sets the aims, principles and tasks of state AI policy to 2030 across priority areas (education and training, science, economy, cybersecurity, information security, defence, public administration, legal regulation and ethics, justice). It identifies problems such as the absence of AI legal regulation and of common ethical approaches, and instructs the Ministry of Digital Transformation with other central executive bodies to prepare an implementation action plan within three months.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Ukraine's current framework AI policy document; the basis for the 2021-2024 action plan and the draft AI Strategy to 2030.

instruments.summary: Cabinet order approving the 2021-2024 action plan for the AI Concept, listing measures with responsible bodies, deadlines and indicators, starting with preparing a Cabinet act approving a concept for an AI development bill (Ministry of Digital Transformation, Q2 2021), AI awareness campaigns in schools and international research cooperation. Ministries and central executive bodies must implement the plan and report annually by 15 January to the Ministry of Digital Transformation, which reports to the Cabinet by 15 February.

instruments.official_title: Проект розпорядження Кабінету Міністрів України «Про схвалення Стратегії розвитку штучного інтелекту в Україні на період до 2030 року та затвердження операційного плану заходів з її реалізації у 2026-2028 роках»
instruments.english_title: Draft Cabinet of Ministers order 'On approval of the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Ukraine until 2030 and approval of the operational action plan for its implementation in 2026-2028'
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: A first draft of the Strategy and of the 2026-2028 operational plan was published for public feedback by the Ministry of Digital Transformation on 31.03.2026 (Ministry news page and AI portal). The formal consultation notice on the draft Cabinet order was published on 15.06.2026, with comments accepted until 30 June 2026; the Ministry's consultation report (one participant, the TELAS telecom operators' association) is published with the draft, the explanatory note and the 2026-2028 operational plan. Not adopted by the Cabinet as of 2026-10-13 (no adopted order found on the Ministry's AI portal or news). Consultation closed on 30 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Draft Cabinet order, put to public consultation by the Ministry of Digital Transformation, that would approve an AI Development Strategy to 2030 with four strategic goals (accelerating AI adoption, developing and widening access to core AI technologies, securing the foundations for AI development, and effective governance for fast and responsible AI adoption) and a 2026-2028 operational plan. The strategy text calls for aligning Ukrainian law with the EU AI Act and designating an AI regulator for market surveillance meeting EU effectiveness and independence criteria; the draft order would repeal the 2020 AI Concept and its action plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed successor to the 2020 AI Concept; would set Ukraine's AI governance direction to 2030.

instruments.summary: Consultation version of the Ministry of Digital Transformation's approach to AI regulation, proposing a two-stage 'bottom-up' approach: first, voluntary tools to prepare business and the state (regulatory sandbox, an AI human-rights impact assessment methodology, sectoral recommendations, voluntary codes of conduct, labelling), then a law analogous to the EU AI Act. instruments.official_title: Дорожня карта з регулювання штучного інтелекту в Україні
instruments.english_title: Roadmap for the regulation of artificial intelligence in Ukraine
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: Presented by the Ministry of Digital Transformation on 7 October 2023 (Government portal news page, published 07.10.2023). The 10-page roadmap is published on the Ministry's file server and listed under 'Інші документи' on its AI portal; the document itself carries no date. Its first stage (White Paper, sectoral recommendations, voluntary code, regulatory sandbox) has been delivered; the AI-law stage is pending (the Ministry announced on 15.06.2026 that a joint working group will draft an AI law during 2026).
instruments.summary: The Ministry of Digital Transformation's roadmap for AI regulation, built on a two-stage 'bottom-up' approach: a first stage of 2-3 years of non-legislative tools (White Paper, regulatory sandbox, HUDERIA human-rights impact assessment, AI labelling, guidance, voluntary commitments and codes of conduct) to prepare industry and build the capacity of a future regulator, then a second stage implementing the EU AI Act, possibly gradually. Its stated goals are business competitiveness and EU market access, protection of human rights from AI risks, a culture of self- and co-regulation, and integration with EU standards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Framework for the Ministry's sequenced, EU-aligned AI regulation programme.

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine
instruments.current_status: Non-binding recommendations with cover dated 'Серпень 2024', announced by the Ministry of Digital Transformation on the Government portal on 7 August 2024 as part of the AI regulation roadmap. They were developed with IT Ukraine, IAB Ukraine, the Ukrainian Bar Association, the National Council of Television and Radio Broadcasting and the State Service for Food Safety and Consumer Protection.
instruments.summary: Sectoral recommendations for creatives and businesses on using AI in advertising without misleading consumers or breaching advertising law. They cover principles of responsible AI use, audience targeting and personalisation, labelling and transparency of AI-generated content, sensitive content and gender equality, information security and personal-data protection, copyright and sui generis rights, unfair competition and self-regulation, with an annex of checklists for choosing AI tools and assessing generated content.

Several laws and government orders, including the data protection law, are still to be read.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was first completed on 13 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass the same day, covering the digital transformation ministry's AI portal document list, Parliament's bills system, the Cabinet, each ministry and each sector regulator. The national legislation portal and the education ministry's site could still not be accessed, so the data protection law and the text of the Convention 108 ratification law could not be read; Ukraine's Convention 108 ratification (Law 2438-VI of 2010) is taken from Parliament's bill record. A deepfake fraud bill, the energy ministry's draft AI concept, the National Bank's discussion paper and the ministry's sandbox are tracked as leads.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). zakon.rada.gov.ua refused connections after 2 documents (curl TLS resets, WebFetch 503, ~15 min of retries); rada.gov.ua bills not reached; mon.gov.ua 403; ai.thedigital.gov.ua list JS-only; cms.thedigital.gov.ua reset; ombudsman search 404. Shared WebSearch limit hit: health, justice, defence, finance, labour, interior ministries and NKEK, AMCU, broadcasting council, NSSMC not searched. Located-only: AI regulation roadmap (2023-10-07 per kmu.gov.ua news; PDF unreadable) and Order 1351-r (from citations). White Paper classed consultation_draft ('consultation version'). Draft Strategy to 2030 (notice 2026-06-15) would repeal 1556-r; adoption not found. Voluntary Code of Conduct (private-sector) lead. Convention 108: Law 2438-VI text unreadable; attached to Convention 108 from the Rada bill 0170 card (2026-10-13), removed from pending_c108. Thin pass 2026-10-13: 8 records re-checked; i-74fb3d85e71d roadmap now reviewed from storage.thedigital.gov.ua PDF (listed on ministry AI portal); i-0c1b871b4de1 (1351-r) still located-only (kmu.gov.ua captcha). 457-r of 09.05.2025 confirmed via SSSCIP Order 154. Added 8 ministry recommendations (dates from covers; portal createdAt CMS dates not used; advertising PDF image-only, read as images) found via ai-web-api.thedigital.gov.ua/page/item/documents, and SSSCIP Order 154 of 2026-02-23 (date and number from SSSCIP news and documents register; PDFs leave them blank). Higher-education recommendations co-issued by MON, recorded under MDT. Rada bills-system card for bill 0170 shows act 2438-VI of 06.07.2010 (Convention 108 ratification) but the act text itself was not read. Not reached: zakon.rada.gov.ua, kmu.gov.ua full texts, mon.gov.ua (403), mev.gov.ua search (403), UkrNDNC catalogue. Units covered: Law: zakon.rada.gov.ua refused all connections again (curl TLS reset; WebFetch 403), so no gazette/portal AI search was possible; data protection law 2297-VI, copyright law 2811-IX (AI-generated objects), Orders 457-r, 320-r, 1351-r and Law 2438-VI remain unread (leads/located-only). No AI-specific law exists; the Ministry of Digital Transformation announced (15.06.2026) that a joint working group will draft one in 2026.; Parliament: Old bills system (w1.c1.rada.gov.ua) reachable: Convention 108 ratification bill 0170 card read (act 2438-VI of 06.07.2010). itd.rada.gov.ua reachable but no search API used; Bill 15379 (AI fraud/deepfakes, reported registered 03.07.2026) found via discovery only - lead. No registered general AI bill found.; Government: Ministry of Digital Transformation: AI portal document list retrieved via its JSON API - 8 further documents recorded (advertising, IP, higher education, responsible development, lawyers, HR, AI agents, psychological support recommendations); AI regulation roadmap now read and upgraded; draft AI Strategy to 2030 still not adopted (first draft 31.03.2026, consultation 15.06.2026). Cabinet: Orders 457-r (confirmed via SSSCIP order), 320-r and the April 2025 MDT-powers resolution are leads (portal unreachable, kmu.gov.ua captcha). Ministry of Energy: draft AI concept for the fuel and energy complex (lead, no dated notice).; Ministries: Education (MON): higher-education recommendations co-authored with MDT recorded; school recommendations remain a draft without stated date (lead); mon.gov.ua 403. Health (MOZ): no AI document found (only news on WHO guidance). Justice: lawyers' recommendations are an MDT document; no separate MoJ instrument found. Defence: only a news item on the A1 Defense AI Center (17.03.2026), no instrument. Finance/tax/customs: only news on AI pilots in customs, no instrument. Labour/social policy: none found (HR recommendations by MDT cover employment). Interior/police: none found. Agriculture: none found. Foreign affairs: none found. Energy: draft AI concept (lead). Strategic industries: Order 320-r programme concept (lead).; Regulators: National Bank of Ukraine: AI page and discussion paper re-read, still no stated date (lead). NSSMC (securities): nothing found. Insurance/non-bank finance is supervised by the NBU: covered by the NBU paper. NKEK (telecoms): nothing found. National Council of Television and Radio Broadcasting: co-developed MDT media/advertising recommendations, no own AI instrument found. Health regulator (State Expert Centre / medicines service): nothing found. NAQA (higher-education quality agency): nothing found. Antimonopoly Committee: nothing found. Ombudsman (data protection authority): 04.06.2024 statement with AI recommendations in a news item only (no document) - not recorded. SSSCIP (cyber): Recommendations on cyber protection of ICS using AI (Order No. 154 of 23.02.2026) recorded. Standards body (UkrNDNC): no national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001/23894/22989 found.. Not reached: zakon.rada.gov.ua (legislation portal: curl TLS reset, WebFetch 403); kmu.gov.ua (captcha for curl; WebFetch works for news only); mon.gov.ua (403); mev.gov.ua search (403); cip.gov.ua document page (WebFetch 403; read through its JSON API instead); itd.rada.gov.ua bill search (not attempted beyond discovery); uas.gov.ua / UkrNDNC standards catalogue (not reached; discovery only). Could not verify: Convention 108 (Law No. 2438-VI): the act text at zakon.rada.gov.ua/laws/show/2438-17 could not be read (curl TLS reset, WebFetch 403). The Verkhovna Rada bills system card for bill 0170 (https://w1.c1.rada.gov.ua/pls/zweb2/webproc4_1?pf3511=37996) was read: 'Проект Закону про ратифікацію Конвенції про захист осіб у зв'язку з автоматизованою обробкою персональних даних та Додаткового протоколу...', registered 16.06.2010 (President), adopted 01.07.2010, act 2438-VI of 06.07.2010. The act itself was not read, so convention108 is null; the lead may accept the bill card if a parliament record suffices.; Law on Personal Data Protection 2297-VI (portal unreachable); Order 457-r of 09.05.2025 text (existence confirmed via SSSCIP Order 154); Order 1351-r text (still located only); Order 320-r of 13.04.2024; Concept 1556-r and Order 438-r could not be re-read in the second pass (portal unreachable); kept from the first-pass reading. binding-law, procurement, standards, index-readiness, international, historical: no material found.
